h2: Vendor inspection and source inspection for US and Canadian buyers
html:
Purchasers use three names for the same job. Vendor inspection and vendor surveillance are the terms in most US and Canadian purchase orders; source inspection is the term API uses in API RP 588 for inspection at the supplier's works before equipment ships; and third party inspection stresses that the inspector works for the buyer, not the fabricator. All three mean that an independent inspector checks the equipment is being built to the purchase order, the code and the approved inspection and test plan (ITP) before it is released.

What a source inspection covers

The scope is set by the ITP and by the level of surveillance the buyer assigns to each order. A typical fixed-equipment visit list includes the pre-inspection meeting, material verification against mill test reports and heat numbers, fit-up and weld visual examination, witness of NDE (radiograph review, UT, MT or PT) or review of the fabricator's NDE reports, dimensional checks against the drawing, the hydrostatic or pneumatic test, coating checks, nameplate and data-report review, and the release note. For rotating equipment the list adds performance and mechanical run tests.

Who should do the inspecting

Many operators now ask for source inspectors who hold an API source inspector certification; the guide to API SIFE vs SIRE explains which one fits fixed and rotating equipment. On weld-heavy orders the inspector also needs to understand the NDE being witnessed well enough to judge technique, calibration and acceptance, which is why an ASNT Level II or Level III background matters there.

Houston and beyond

The Houston area builds a large share of the oilfield, refinery and petrochemical equipment bought in North America, so it is where buyers most often need vendor inspection. The same inspectors travel to supplier works elsewhere in the US and in Canada when orders are placed there. On Canadian orders, the ITP will usually add a check of the provincial design registration (CRN) and of CSA B51 requirements for boilers and pressure vessels. For large orders, a resident inspector can be assigned for the length of the contract, as described above.

Related services

Field NDE on the same equipment once it is installed is covered by NDT inspection services and API 510 pressure vessel inspection. Program-level help with ITPs, procedures and supplier qualification sits with NDT supplier audits. To place a vendor inspection order, send the purchase order, ITP and delivery date.
